title: Universal Design for Learning (UDL) Accessibility Pass
problem: Course materials designed for a single 'default' learner — one reading level, one format, one pace — routinely underserve students with disabilities, English-language learners, and anyone outside the instructor's original assumptions. A full UDL redesign of an entire course is too time-consuming to do from scratch for every lesson.

workflow.step: 1. Pick one lesson and state its outcome
workflow.detail: UDL passes work best applied lesson-by-lesson, not to a whole syllabus at once.

workflow.step: 2. Audit against the three UDL principles
workflow.detail: Run the Prompt Template to check the current material for multiple means of engagement, representation, and action/expression.
The model will likely surface more gaps than you can fix before the next class. Pick the 1–2 highest-impact fixes for your actual student population.

workflow.step: 4. Generate alternatives for just those fixes
workflow.detail: E.g. an audio version of a reading, a scaffolded worked example, or a choice of output format for the assignment.

A UDL pass improves pedagogy but does not substitute for your institution's actual accessibility/ADA review — captioning, screen-reader testing, and documented accommodations still need their own process.

variables.name: OUTCOME
variables.label: Learning outcome
variables.placeholder: e.g. Interpret coefficients and p-values in a regression table

variables.name: CURRENT_MATERIALS
variables.label: Current materials & format
variables.placeholder: e.g. 20-slide lecture deck + a single dense reading, no alternative formats

variables.name: STUDENT_NEEDS
variables.label: Known student needs (optional)
variables.placeholder: e.g. Two students with documented extended-time accommodations; several multilingual learners

exampleOutput:
**Gaps found:**
- Representation: Only one dense text reading covers the concept — no visual or audio alternative.
- Action/expression: The homework only accepts a written proof; no option to demonstrate the skill via a worked walkthrough or short recorded explanation.

**Ranked top 2 fixes:**
1. Add a 5-minute annotated-example video alongside the reading (representation).
2. Offer a choice: written proof OR a short recorded walkthrough of the same problem (action/expression).
tips: Apply this lesson-by-lesson, not to the whole course at once — a full-course UDL rewrite is a project, not a single prompt.
This recipe improves pedagogical design; it does not replace your institution's formal accessibility review for students with documented accommodations.
If STUDENT_NEEDS is unknown, leave it blank and ask for a general UDL best-practice audit rather than letting the model invent assumptions about your students.
Local LLMs (Ollama) work fine here since the audit is reasoning over text you provide, not requiring broad world knowledge — a good low-cost option to run per-lesson.
